answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to slashable stake and a history of randomly sampled cross-agent tasks. New identities start with little influence, while useful agents gain reputation only when independent peers verify their work; conflicting reports trigger audits that burn the stake. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and solve costly tasks before gaining power, so a swarm demands capital and time, even when spread across a mesa, quartz mine, or reef.
